QF.id: Cat III AIF Overview and Growth_29

question.text: Category III AIFs are 'more suited' to investors who:

answer.text: Are institutional or UHNI investors with high risk appetite, at least Rs. 1 crore capital commitment, and the ability to tolerate the fund's tenure/lock-in and redemption terms

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 37-39 of the source describe Category III AIFs as suited to institutional or UHNI investors with high risk tolerance. Page 38 explicitly states that a one-year horizon is infeasible and that closed-ended Category III AIFs carry a minimum three-year tenure with a generally two-year lock-in. Page 51 supports the Rs. 1 crore minimum commitment. The Trap: Daily-liquidity needs, retiree-style income profiles and capital-protection mandates do not match the risk, tenure and ticket-size profile of Category III AIFs. Note: When describing suitability, retain the specific three-year tenure / two-year lock-in language from page 38 rather than a generic "2+ years" framing.
